content: How can you contribute to WikiDoc? Thank you for your interest in WikiDoc, the Living Global Textbook of Medicine. Below are detailed ways you can assist in providing the world with the highest quality and most up-to-date medical information. If you have any questions, comments, or suggestions about contributing to WikiDoc, please feel free to contact Scott Williams. Submit Copyleft Images Upload USMLE Step II Images: Follow the specific instructions provided in the How to upload USMLE II Images guide to upload these images. Upload Images from Gray's Anatomy: Visit the List of images and subjects in Gray's Anatomy and upload any missing images from Wikipedia. Upload Pathology Videos from Ask Dr Wiki: Contribute by uploading relevant pathology videos. Upload Images from the PEIR Digital Library: This is a pathology image database. When uploading images from the PEIR database, ensure you include the appropriate citation below the image. Refer to the Normoblast page for an example of how the citation should appear. Contribute Your Own Copyleft Images: Share your original images under a copyleft license. Refer to Help: Images and Other Media: Use this resource for detailed instructions on how to upload images. Write a WikiDoc News Article Share Newsworthy Information: If you come across any newsworthy medical information, share it with WikiDoc's users. Follow the News Team Resources: Refer to WikiDoc News: News Team Resources for instructions on how to write a WikiDoc news article. Use the WikiDoc News Template: This template provides an example of how a WikiDoc news article should be structured. Post Your News Article: Once your article is written, follow the How to post a WikiDoc News article guide to publish it on the front page of WikiDoc. Link Medical Terms: Ensure that medical terms in your article are linked to their respective pages in the WikiDoc Global Textbook of Medicine by using double brackets (e.g., [[term]]). Insert Patient Resource Links Add Useful External Links: If you know of a website that provides accurate and reliable information about a specific disease, insert a link in the External Links section of the relevant WikiDoc page. Use a Standard Template: Follow the provided template for inserting and titling the link. Create an External Links Section: If the page does not already have an External Links section, feel free to create one. Edit a Page Awaiting Pre-Medical Review Select a Page to Edit: Go to the Category: Awaiting pre-medical review and choose a page to edit. Add medically relevant content to sections currently linked in red. Follow Editing Guidelines: Do not overwrite the original content of pages that include extensive differential diagnoses with a Wikipedia page. Ensure the {{pmr}} template is at the top of the page. Check the page history to confirm there is no extensive differential diagnosis or other text created by Heather Mangan or Caitlin Harrigan. If such content exists, integrate it appropriately. Create links from as many parts of the differential diagnosis as possible. Ensure the page is categorized appropriately. End the page with the following templates: {{WikiDoc Help Menu}} and {{WikiDoc Sources}}. Complete Your Review: Once you finish reviewing the page, replace the {{pmr}} template with {{jb1}}. This will prompt a bot to remove any remaining red links.
